sanskrit: na tatra dhenur duhe nānaḍvān sahate dhuram | vijānir yatra brāhmaṇo rātriṃ vasati pāpayā ||
english: There the cow gives no milk, the ox does not bear the yoke — in the house where a brāhmaṇa spends the night in misery, knowing full well.

sanskrit: na varṣaṃ maitrāvaruṇaṃ brahmajyam abhi varṣati | nāsmai samitiḥ kalpate na mitraṃ nayate vaśam ||
english: The rain of Mitra and Varuṇa does not rain down upon one who has wronged a brāhmaṇa; for him the assembly does not convene auspiciously, nor does he bring an ally under his sway.

sanskrit: asṛṅmatī carati brahmajāyā āśā limpantī pradiśaś catasraḥ | yaḥ kṣatriyaḥ punar enāṃ dadāti sa divo dhārāṃ dhayati prapīnām ||
english: The wife of a brāhmaṇa wanders blood-stained, staining the hopes and the four quarters of the sky; but that kṣatriya who restores her sucks the swelling stream of heaven.

sanskrit: yo 'punardāya brahmajāyāṃ rājā talpe nipadyate | duryoṇā asmā oṣadhīr yāḥ kāś cābhi vipaśyati ||
english: The king who, without having restored the brāhmaṇa's wife, lies down upon his couch — for him the herbs that he looks upon from any direction become dwelling-places of ill omen.

sanskrit: viṣam aśnāty apāṃ viṣam aśnāti vīrudhām | yo brahmajāyāṃ na punar dadāti tasmai devāḥ sudihaṃ digdham asyām ||
english: He eats the poison of the waters, he eats the poison of the plants — he who does not restore the brāhmaṇa's wife; upon him the gods smear what is well-smeared with venom in her.

sanskrit: udyat patayo daśa striyāḥ pūrve abrāhmaṇāḥ | brahmā ced dhastam agrahīt sa eva patir ekadhā ||
english: Though ten former husbands of a woman may be non-brāhmaṇas, if a brāhmaṇa has taken her hand, he alone is her husband in a singular sense.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇa eva patir na rājā nota vaiśyaḥ | tat sūryaḥ prabruvann eti pañcabhyo mānavebhyaḥ ||
english: The brāhmaṇa alone is the husband — not the king, nor the vaiśya. Thus does the sun declare, going forth to the five tribes of men.

sanskrit: naitāṃ te devā adadus tubhyaṃ nṛpate attave | mā brāhmaṇasya rājanya gāṃ jighatso anādyām ||
english: O king, the gods did not give her to you to devour; O prince, do not desire to consume the cow of a brāhmaṇa — she is not to be eaten.

sanskrit: akṣadrugdho rājanyaḥ pāpa ātmaparājitaḥ | sa brāhmaṇasya gām adyād adya jīvāni mā śvaḥ ||
english: The prince who has transgressed at dice, evil and self-defeated — let him eat the brāhmaṇa's cow today: "may I live today, not tomorrow."

sanskrit: nir vai kṣatraṃ nayati hanti varco 'gnir ivārabdhaḥ pra dunoti rāṣṭram | yo brāhmaṇaṃ devabandhuṃ hinasti na sa pitṝṇām apy eti lokam ||
english: It truly destroys kingly power, slays splendour; once seized, like fire it torments the realm — he who harms a brāhmaṇa, companion of the gods, reaches not even the world of the ancestors.

sanskrit: devapīyuś carati martyeṣu garagīrṇo bhavaty asthibhūyān | yo brāhmaṇaṃ manyate annam eva sa viṣasya pibati taimātasya ||
english: He who despises the gods walks among mortals; swallowed by poison, he becomes a pile of bones — he who regards the brāhmaṇa as mere food drinks of the primal venom.

sanskrit: viṣaṃ sa pibati taimātaṃ paśyann agniṃ pra sīdati | yo brāhmaṇasya sad dhanam abhi nārada manyate ||
english: He drinks primal poison; looking upon fire he sinks down — he who covets the rightful wealth of a brāhmaṇa, O Nārada.

sanskrit: śatāpāṣṭhāṃ ni girati tāṃ na śaknoti niṣkhidam | annaṃ yo brahmaṇāṃ malvaḥ svādv admīti manyate ||
english: He swallows one bearing a hundred sharp thorns, and cannot spit it out — the wretch who thinks he is pleasantly eating the brāhmaṇas' sweet food.

sanskrit: ya enāṃ hanti mṛdu manyamāno devapīyur dhanakāmo na cittāt | saṃ tasyendro hṛdaye agnim indha ubhe enaṃ dyuṣṭo nabhasī carantam ||
english: He who strikes her down, thinking it easy — a god-scorner, greedy for wealth, without discernment — Indra kindles fire in his heart; on both sides the heavens, by day, pursue him as he wanders.

sanskrit: na brāhmaṇo hiṃsitavā agneḥ priyatamā tanūḥ | somo hy asya dāyāda indro asyābhiśastipāḥ ||
english: The brāhmaṇa must not be harmed — he is the dearest embodiment of Agni; for Soma is his hereditary protector and Indra his guardian against denunciation.

sanskrit: agnir vai naḥ padavāyaḥ somo dāyāda ucyate | jetā abhiśastendras tat satyaṃ devasaṃhitam ||
english: Agni is indeed our tracker, Soma is called the hereditary guardian, Indra the vanquisher of calumny — that is the truth, the divine compact.

sanskrit: āviṣṭitāghaviṣā pṛdākūr iva carmaṇā | sā brāhmaṇasya rājanya tṛṣṭaiṣā gaur anādyā ||
english: Filled with deadly venom like a pṛdākū serpent beneath its skin — that is the brāhmaṇa's cow, O prince: she is fierce, inedible.

sanskrit: iṣur iva digdhā nṛpate pṛdākūr iva gopate | sā brāhmaṇasyeṣur digdhā tayā vidhyati pīyakaḥ ||
english: Like a poisoned arrow, O king; like a pṛdākū serpent, O lord of cattle — the brāhmaṇa's arrow is venomed, and with it he pierces the reviler.

sanskrit: tīkṣṇeṣavo brāhmaṇā hetimanto yām asyanti śaravyāṃ na sā mṛṣā | anuhāya tapasā manyunā cota dūrād ava bhindanti te tayā ||
english: Brāhmaṇas have sharp arrows and weapons; the target they aim at is never missed — releasing with tapas and with wrath, from afar they shatter with that arrow.

sanskrit: jihvā jyā bhavati kulmalaṃ vāṅ nāḍīkā dantās tapasā sudigdhāḥ | tebhir brahmā vidhyati devapīyūn hṛdbalair dhanurbhir devajūtaiḥ ||
english: The tongue becomes the bowstring, speech the arrow-shaft, the teeth are reeds well-smeared with tapas — with these, the brahman-power pierces those who scorn the gods, with god-impelled bows whose force resides in the heart.

sanskrit: ye brāhmaṇaṃ hiṃsitāras tapasvinaṃ manīṣiṇaṃ brahmacaryeṇa śrāntam | avartimad bhavitā rāṣṭram eṣāṃ tamasīva nihitaṃ nānu vettāḥ ||
english: Those who would harm a brāhmaṇa — the ascetic, the wise, the one worn by celibate discipline — their kingdom shall become unstable; like something placed in darkness, it shall be known no more.

sanskrit: ye sahasram arājann āsan daśaśatā uta | te brāhmaṇasya gāṃ jagdhvā vaitahavyāḥ parābhavan ||
english: Those who were a thousand, O king, those who were a full ten hundred — the Vaitahavyas perished, having devoured the brāhmaṇa's cow.

sanskrit: gaur eva tān hanyamānā vaitahavyām̐ avātirat | ye keśara prābandhāyāś caramājām apeciran ||
english: The cow herself, being slaughtered, overthrew those Vaitahavyas — those who had stripped away the last she-goat of the one bound by the hair.

sanskrit: atimātrā ajāyanta nod iva divam aspṛśan | bhṛguṃ hiṃsitvā māhīnā asaṃbhavyaṃ parābhavan ||
english: They were born beyond measure, like a thunderbolt they almost touched the sky — yet having harmed Bhṛgu, the Māhīnas perished beyond all recovery.

sanskrit: ye bṛhatsāmānam āṅgirasam ārpayan brāhmaṇaṃ janāḥ | yetvas teṣām ubhayādann avis tokāny āvayat ||
english: The people who aimed at the Āṅgirasa brāhmaṇa, the singer of the Bṛhatsāman — the sheep gnawed away the offspring of those ambidextrous assailants.

sanskrit: ye brāhmaṇaṃ pratyaṣṭhīvan ye cāsmic chuklam īṣire | asnas te madhye kulyāyāḥ keśān khādanta āsate ||
english: Those who spat at the brāhmaṇa, and those who cast their white at him — they sit in the midst of a stream of blood, eating hair.

sanskrit: aṣṭāpadī caturakṣī catuḥśrotrā caturhanuḥ | dvijihvā dviprāṇā bhūtvā sā rāṣṭram ava dhūnute ||
english: Having become eight-footed, four-eyed, four-eared, four-jawed, double-tongued, double-breathed — she shakes the kingdom to its ruin.
